haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes. Then it lapses to EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale, unless the order claimed it first. A lapsed hold can still be claimed if every line is free again.
haiku-low.q2: Before. Inventory reserves all lines first. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, and the order is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK with the short items shown.
haiku-low.q3: The idempotency key, which is the order id. The provider treats a retried charge with the same key as the same request, and Payment retries with that key.
haiku-low.q4: The customer gets a full refund. The order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is emailed, and a refund is requested and tracked until REFUNDED or REFUND_STUCK.
haiku-low.q5: Only after OrderConfirmed, when Cart empties it on that event. If checkout fails before CONFIRMED, the cart is never emptied, so the customer can try again.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service coordinates, deciding the next step after each reply or event. Its orders table holds each checkout's status.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment records the outcome and emits PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined through its outbox to the broker, which Order consumes.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores the provider event id in processed_webhooks with a unique constraint, in the same transaction as the update. Repeats get 200 and are ignored. Consumers use processed_events, and status guards block a second transition.
haiku-low.q9: Payment emits PaymentDeclined. Order marks PAYMENT_DECLINED, emails the customer, and tells Inventory to release the hold, so the stock goes back on sale.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory accepts the claim if the hold is still HELD, or lapsed but every line can be reserved again now. Otherwise it refuses and the order is cancelled with a full refund.
haiku-low.q11: The refund stays REFUND_PENDING and is retried with backoff using the same key. After N tries it becomes REFUND_STUCK, on-call is alerted, and retries continue. It is tracked in the refunds table.
haiku-low.q12: Order emits OrderConfirmed after confirming. Cart service handles that event and empties the cart.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If not claimed, it lapses to EXPIRED (a timer runs every minute) and the stock goes back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging; payment is requested only after stock is held. If any line is short, nothing is reserved (all or nothing), no payment is requested, and the order becomes REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK with the short items shown.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key: the order id is sent with the charge, so the provider treats a retry as the same request. Payment retries with the same key.
sonnet.q4: The claim is refused; Order marks it CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer, and requests a full refund via RefundRequested. Payment refunds the full amount.
sonnet.q5: Emptied only after the order is CONFIRMED (on the OrderConfirmed event), and only then. On any failure before CONFIRMED the cart is left untouched so the customer can try again.
sonnet.q6: The Order service is the coordinator, deciding the next step after each reply or event. The record of progress is the order's status in Order's orders table (PLACED, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, etc.).
sonnet.q7: The provider calls Payment by webhook; Payment updates the payment and sends a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event via its outbox and the broker to Order.
sonnet.q8: Payment inserts the provider event id into processed_webhooks (unique) in the same transaction as the payment update; a repeat hits the unique constraint and is acknowledged with 200 and ignored. Status guards (only PENDING can transition) also stop a second transition. Consumers of broker messages record ids in processed_events.
sonnet.q9: The hold is released so stock goes back on sale. Triggered by the PaymentDeclined event: Order marks PAYMENT_DECLINED, emails the customer, and makes an HTTP release call to Inventory.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim. Inventory accepts if the hold is still HELD, or if it lapsed but every line can be reserved again right now (checked in one row transaction). Otherwise the claim is refused and the order is cancelled and refunded.
sonnet.q11: The refund stays REFUND_PENDING and is retried with backoff using the same key. After N tries it becomes REFUND_STUCK, on-call is alerted, and retries continue on a slow schedule. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table (status, attempts, next_retry_at), and Order shows the refund status on the order record.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, emitted by Order through its outbox after confirming, causes the Cart service to empty the cart.
